Roofing in Hurst, Texas

Much of Hurst was built in a rush in the 1950s and 1960s, and the city asks roofers for ID and insurance on each permit. One free number, answered any hour, connects you with an independent roofer that takes Hurst calls.

Call (469) 649-7066 Hurst permit paperwork

  2. Service Areas
  3. Hurst

A town that went up in a hurry

Roofing in Hurst, TX starts with the town's age. The city's own history says the Bell helicopter plant, begun in 1951, touched off a building boom, and Hurst incorporated on September 25, 1952 with about 2,700 people.

Growth did not slow. The city counts roughly 5,700 residents five years after incorporation, about 10,000 by 1960 and more than 27,000 by 1970. A 1953 Fort Worth Star-Telegram photo in the UTA archive shows rows of new houses going up and notes that land values had climbed 200 to 1,000 percent. A 1955 aerial view looking south from Pipeline Road already shows Highway 183, Brown Trail and the Bell plant. North East Mall followed in 1972.

What that means today: many Hurst houses are past their sixtieth birthday. Their roofs have been replaced before, sometimes more than once, and each time someone made choices about decking, layers and vents that the next roofer inherits. DFW Expert Roofers does not inspect any of it. Its job is narrower: answer the phone for free and hand your call to an independent, locally owned roofing company working in Hurst, which takes it from there.

How Hurst handles roofing permits now

Hurst changed how it tracks contractors. Instead of a yearly sign-up, the paperwork rides along with each permit. Here is what the Building Inspections pages describe.

ItemWhat the city saysWhat to ask your roofer
Contractor registrationNo annual registration. The contractor registers on each permit application.Will you pull the permit for my job, under your company name?
Documents with the permitA copy of a US-issued ID, a trade license if applicable, and a copy of general liability insurance.May I see the same insurance certificate you give the city?
Where it is filedThe online Citizen Self-Service portal, using a company name and company email, not a personal one.What is the permit number once it is issued?
Roof sign-offThe city's permit resources include a Roof Contractors page and a Certificate of Final Roof Installation/Inspection form.Who files the final roof certificate, and will I get a copy?
Homeowner permitsAllowed only when the owner lives in the house and does the work personally.Not a fit for roof work; let the roofer pull it.

One loose end: a Public Works fee page still lists a yearly contractor registration fee, which does not match the per-permit process. If anything is unclear about your job, Building Inspections answers at 817-788-7088.

What a careful roofer looks at on a mid-century Hurst roof

How many layers are up there

A house roofed in the 1950s or 1960s has had several roofs. If one was laid over another, the weight and the hidden decking both matter. Ask the roofer to count the layers and write the number down.

The decking under the shingles

Decking on an older house may be original. Only a tear-off shows whether it is sound. Ask what one replacement sheet costs before work starts, so a surprise does not become a fight.

Vents, pipes and chimneys

Decades of remodeling add vents and pipe boots in odd places, and older chimneys carry their own flashing. Leaks often start at those spots rather than in the open field of shingles.

Attic airflow

A roof that cannot breathe runs hot under a North Texas summer sun. Ask the roofer to check the attic's intake and exhaust vents and say whether the quote changes them.

Leave the roof to the roofer. A wet or storm-hit roof is slippery, and damaged decking can give way, so keep off it and keep the ladder put away. Stay clear of any downed power line and report it to Oncor or your local electric utility, or call 911. Inside, pull furniture and electronics away from the drip, set out a bucket or towels, and keep everyone out of a room where the ceiling is sagging. Take photos from the yard and from inside, then call your insurance company and a roofer.

Before you sign with a roofer in Hurst

  • Ask for the general liability certificate to be sent to you by the roofer's insurance agent, the same coverage the city asks for on the permit.
  • Confirm the company name on the contract matches the name on the Hurst permit.
  • Get the layer count, the decking price per sheet and the underlayment by product name in writing.
  • Ask who files the city's final roof certificate and when you will see it.
  • For an insurance job, read the deductible notice in the contract. Texas requires it.

Your deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance warns that a contractor may not waive your deductible, rebate it, or pad the estimate to cover it, and that a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice that you owe the deductible. Your insurer may ask for proof you paid it. A contractor also may not act as a public adjuster on a property it works on or may work on. If a roofer offers to "take care of" the deductible, hire someone else.

No state license for roofers. Texas does not license roofing contractors. A 2025 bill that would have had the state license re-roofers (HB 3344) cleared a House committee but never got a floor vote, and it died when the session ended. That puts the checking on you: ask for a certificate of liability insurance sent to you by the roofer's insurance agent or insurer, a written contract that lists the full scope, the permit or contractor registration your city requires, addresses of nearby jobs, and proof the shingle warranty was registered. The line does none of this checking for you. How to check a roofer in Texas.

What happens when you call from Hurst

  1. Dial the lineAn automated assistant picks up (469) 649-7066 any time and asks what you need. The same number also takes air conditioning, heating and pressure washing calls, so say "roof".
  2. Tell it about the roofHail, a drip in the ceiling, shingles in the yard, a tree limb, or an aging roof you want checked, plus your town and how soon you need someone.
  3. Get transferredThe call goes to an independent roofing company that is locally owned and works in Dallas-Fort Worth. It hears a quick summary of your call before it answers.
  4. Work with that companyIt inspects, prices and does the job, and you pay it (or your insurer does, as you arrange). If it cannot pick up, it gets your name, number, town and need so it can call you back.

The line itself charges nothing and holds no license. It answers, asks a few questions, and passes your call or your details to the roofer.

Water stain on a ceiling in an older Hurst house, or shingles in the yard after a storm? Call and describe it. Whichever Hurst roofer picks up will look over the house itself and price the job on paper.

Roofing questions from Hurst

Does Hurst make roofing contractors register?

Not once a year anymore. The Building Inspections department says Hurst dropped annual contractor registration, and a contractor now registers through each permit application by sending a copy of a US-issued ID, a trade license if one applies, and a copy of its general liability insurance. A separate city fee page still mentions a yearly registration, so if the two disagree, call Building Inspections at 817-788-7088.

Who do I call for hurst roof repair after a storm?

For a roof that is leaking or missing shingles, call the free line. An automated assistant asks what happened and transfers you to an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes Hurst calls, and if that company cannot pick up it gets your details for a call back. Until someone arrives, stay off the roof and catch drips inside. Our roof leak repair page covers what to expect.

Can a Hurst homeowner pull a roofing permit on their own?

Only in a narrow case. The city says a homeowner may pull a permit without a contractor when the homeowner lives in the house and personally does the work. Roof work is not a job to take on yourself, so in practice the roofer should pull the permit under its own company account, and its name should match the contract.

Should a 1950s or 1960s Hurst house get a full tear-off?

Often a roofer will suggest one, but ask to see why. Homes from Hurst's early boom have usually been re-roofed more than once, and a tear-off lets the roofer see the decking and count any old layers. Ask for the decking and layer count in writing. The roof replacement page explains the steps of a tear-off.

Roof trouble in Hurst? Call the free line

Say what the roof is doing and which town you are in. The automated assistant passes you to an independent roofing company that is locally owned and works in DFW. That company comes out, looks at the roof and prices the job itself.
